Oh, and Derrick Henry will look to run all over his former team in the Tennessee Titans . That's a must-watch revenge game. Let's discuss some anytime touchdown bets. These have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Last week, we hit on Tee Higgins at +175 and tight end Harold Fannin Jr . at +235. Let's see what we have cooking up for Week 4. Below, we will break down five anytime TD bets to consider. These will not be predictable choices like a Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson score that offer zero value, but they won't be wild long shots such as a team defense. Let's begin with a tight end who looked incredible last week in his 2026 debut. Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook. 1. Raiders TE Brock Bowers (+160) The Las Vegas Raiders have a massive matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs this week. The Raiders are off to a surprising 3-0 start, although we can't ignore the fact that they've played the easiest strength of schedule in the NFL up to this point, as their first three opponents have won one game combined. Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers made his season debut last week against the New Orleans Saints , and he looked magnificent. He caught a game-high 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown in a 35-27 win, and will be important if the Raiders want to score an upset victory over their rivals. With how good Bowers looked last week, I'll sprinkle on him again in this spot as Kirk Cousins ' new clear-cut "WR1." 2. Bills RB James Cook (-140) James Cook of the Buffalo Bills is one of the best running backs in the NFL, and he's on a bit of a heater right now. He rushed 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 vs. the Detroit Lions , and then 24 times for 154 yards and another touchdown last week against the Los Angeles Chargers . Now, the flailing New England Patriots come to town, and they are missing two important defenders in Christian Barmore and Christian Gonzalez . They lost by 29 points to the Jacksonville Jaguars last week, and I'm sure Joe Brady and the Bills want to do something similar to the team that won their division last year. A -140 price isn't value, but I can tell you I was surprised by this listing. 3. Vikings RB Aaron Jones (-160) Like James Cook, this line doesn't offer much value. But consider that the Miami Dolphins have allowed six touchdowns to running backs through three games. The Minnesota Vikings are favored by double-digits over Miami, which makes sense because the Dolphins just lost De'Von Achane for the year, while Brian Flores is going to look to DESTROY his former team from a defensive standpoint. That means Aaron Jones is going to get plenty of touches. He hasn't scored since Week 1, but will in Week 4. 4. Jets RB Braelon Allen (+115) I was a fan of Braelon Allen in the 2024 draft process because he's big at 6-foot-1, 235 pounds, and was the youngest player in the entire class. He actually racked up 482 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns as a rookie, but an injury held him to four games played last year. Now, he's making his third career start with Breece Hall sidelined by a quad injury. When the New York Jets get in the red zone against the Chicago Bears , Frank Reich is going to call his number. 5. Saints RB Alvin Kamara (+135) (Monday) This game is on Monday night, but I had to mention it. The Saints are hosting the Atlanta Falcons in the 20th anniversary of the "Rebirth Game," where the Saints returned to the Superdome for the first time following Hurricane Katrina. The legendary Steve Gleason blocked a punt on the opening drive of the game, which set the tone for an emotional 23-3 Saints victory. I can't imagine what the environment will be like on Monday night. Travis Etienne is out with a hamstring injury, opening the door for franchise legend Alvin Kamara . He's not as productive as he used to be, but it makes too much sense for him to score in this game. Bonus: Ravens RB Derrick Henry 2 TDs (+250) Derrick Henry faces the team that selected him No. 45 overall in the 2016 NFL Draft this Sunday. Henry and the Titans didn't have some dramatic breakup, but Henry wanted to win football games and the Titans were about to suffer an embarrassing fall to the bottom of the league, so a mutual parting of ways made sense. It used to be a debate if Henry was a future Hall of Famer. Not anymore. The ageless wonder leads the NFL with 3,817 rushing yards and 38 rushing touchdowns since signing with the Baltimore Ravens in 2024. Those are more rushing yards and more rushing touchdowns than the entire Titans offense since he left. Derrick Henry to find the end zone at -210 is probably a parlay leg, but what about two touchdowns at +250? He's averaging two touchdowns a game this year as it is! Imagine telling someone after Week 1 the Browns and Deshaun Watson would be 3-1. You could be holding a Gray's Sporting Almanac and they wouldn't believe you. Bet on the NFL and more at DraftKings, where new users get $150 in bonus bets after spending $5+: So let's continue to expect the unexpected as we head into the meat of Week 4 and let's not do what, ahem, some of us did last week, which is to take too much road chalk. It's been bad for a while and will likely continue to be. Just when you think a team is down and out, they might be ready to surprise you. Let's find some winners, as well as some good player props and touchdown scorers! Best bets for NFL Week 4 Jets +3.5 at Bears The Bears were an incredible story in Week 3, with Case Keenum delivering an elite primetime performance to steal a win over the Eagles and help propel Chicago's season forward despite Caleb Williams ' injury. I think he can play well here too, but I also think the Bears being a 3.5-point favorite is a bit too much against a Jets team that has been pretty darn frisky so far this season. This smells like a sneaky shootout to me and when there are a ton of points being scored, I want the hook, especially with the Bears defense being susceptible to teams covering through the backdoor. Chargers +7 at Seahawks I don't think the Chargers are that good, honestly. The offensive line's been terrible, Ladd McConkey might not play and the Seahawks are (were?) a truck and now they're mad and at home. But this line wouldn't have been seven before the season, so it's a pretty massive overcorrection. The Chargers are 0-3 and DESPERATE. They gave the Bills a good run for their money and still didn't cover, so no one's going to be backing them here. I think they'll do the same with Seattle, except the Seahawks won't pull away like Buffalo did. Broncos +3 at 49ers The Broncos either just hang around or find a way to storm back in the second half. They don't care if you have an elite defense or the game is on the road. And we're getting a full three points here, which makes them pretty enticing. We're also coming off a nothing burger from Jaylen Waddle , which means there should be a roll back the other way to feature him heavily on offense. When Waddle's involved, the Broncos offense cooks and Davis Webb will be politely instructed to feature him here. Sean Payton would love nothing more than to beat Sean McVay and Kyle Shanahan in back-to-back weeks and remind everyone who the smartest guy in football really is. Jaguars +2.5 at Bengals Is the wrong team favored here? I know the game is in Cincinnati and the Bengals should be stung off an embarrassing loss to the Steelers . But the Jaguars might own a claim to being the best team in football. Outside of the second half against Denver in Week 2 they've been completely dominant and this Bengals defense, while improved, is not exactly elite. I see a big game from Trevor Lawrence coming here. I can't give out two touchdowns here (but will be putting it in a two-touchdown parlay) and the line is a little steep for my liking, so we'll just back The King to go for 100 yards against the team that drafted him, threw him on the scrap heap and now has defensive players talking trash about him. Ja'Marr Chase Over 83.5 receiving yards This number has flown up over the past few days and might continue to climb. We're expecting a shootout and while I think the Jaguars win, I also think Chase eats in this game. A healthy Joe Burrow means Chase is going to keep having monster games. Davante Adams has picked up the slack and then some in his absence, but Nacua's return to the field should mean the Rams offense upgrades significantly. It also should mean Matthew Stafford targeting him in the red zone again. I think he scores his first touchdown of the year this week and at plus money, it's great value. Brock Bowers (+160) Bowers at 2-1 to score a touchdown? In this economy?? Are you kidding me? Bowers made his season debut last week and put on a freaking route-running clinic in Klint Kubiak's offense. He's his "new JSN" and can be deployed anytime, anywhere, anyhow. I love this bet more than I love most of my family members. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (-130) Speaking of JSN ... he's also way too cheap! It's not plus money, but he's just costing a little bit of juice to score despite finding the end zone six times in three games already this season. Some regression probably happens, but I don't see why it's now, especially with the Seahawks run game being banged up, plenty of points to be scored and JSN playing like the best wide receiver in football. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders – 9:30 am ET (London) The Colts might be down Alec Pierce, but I like the way this offense operates. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. He’s also up against a Colts defense that is 30th in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.124). Honestly, this might not seem like the most enticing standalone game, but I think it’s going to deliver some early-morning excitement. Two shaky defenses should mean a real shot at a shootout. Also, since 2024, the Over is 15-1 when Washington is an underdog of 3.5 to 9.5 points. The average total points scored in such games is 58.2 points per game. Bet: Over 46.5 (-115) Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans – 1:00 pm ET We haven’t seen anything from Houston this season, but a bounce-back performance should be coming soon. I don’t expect the Texans to completely stifle a good Cowboys offense, but I do know that Houston is much better than its No. 19 ranking in EPA/Play Allowed (0.012) this year. This is a Texans defense that has been elite for years, and none of the moves made in the offseason should have resulted in this type of drop-off. That said, look for Houston to start playing some much better defense, and we could see it start with a decent showing against Dak Prescott and Co. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). The Cowboys made some moves to address their miserable defense from last season, but it doesn’t look like any of them have worked. So, this should be a pretty strong matchup for CJ Stroud. Of course, Stroud has issues as a passer, but he’s reliable when he has time to get his feet set. That’s a good thing as Stroud prepares to face a defense that is 31st in Pass Rush Win Rate (40%). He should have plenty of time. This is also a massive desperation spot for Houston. I can’t imagine Dallas is thrilled to be sitting at 1-2 right now, but Houston’s season might be over if the team drops this one to fall to 0-4. Bet: Texans ML (-136) Arizona Cardinals at New York Giants – 1:00 pm ET Jameis Winston has been pretty buttoned up since taking over for Jaxson Dart, but I imagine he’ll be slinging it around a bit here. This season, the Cardinals are allowing 247.0 passing yards per game, and their two starting corners have an average PFF grade of 52.1. New York has been conservative with Winston so far, opting to lean heavily into a ground-and-pound approach. However, the Giants need to play the matchup, and this is one that calls for some passing. Arizona is a top-10 team in pass frequency. So, if the Cardinals are letting Jacoby Brissett air it out, the Giants will have no choice but to let Winston do the same. I know Winston hasn’t yet thrown for a score, and he also hasn’t eclipsed 118 passing yards in a game. But we all know that Winston is a gunslinger, and you don’t have to go back too far to find a box score in which he threw for 366 yards and two touchdowns. That was November 23, 2025, when Winston got involved in a shootout with the Lions. highlights: Best NFL Prop Bets Today for Week 4 (Bet on David Montgomery in Battle of Texas) Week 4 of the NFL season has begun and we have a loaded slate of games to watch and bet on today. If you haven't already placed a few bets on player props, now is your chance. In this article, I'm going to give you a few of our favorites that we've written about throughout the week. Best NFL Prop Bets Today Geno Smith OVER 21.5 Completions (+103) via Caesars David Montgomery OVER 10.5 Receiving Yards (-117) via DraftKings Bryce Young OVER 249.5 Passing Yards (-111) via DraftKings Geno Smith OVER 21.5 Completions (+103) In this week' edition of the Player Prop Countdown, I ranked Geno Smith going over 21.1 completions as my No. 4-ranked prop for Week 4: Geno Smith has been impressive to start the season, despite the Jets being 1-2 through the first three weeks.

Bryce Young OVER 249.5 Passing Yards (-111) If you're looking for a prop bet for Sunday Night Football, Peter Dewey wrote in his Lions vs. Panthers player prop story why he's backing Bryce Young to have a big game: I love this line for Carolina quarterback Bryce Young, who has thrown for over 250 yards in each of his first three games this season. Young has 361, 287, and 291 yards in his three games, and Carolina is 13th in the NFL in EPA/Pass. Young has attempted at least 36 passes in each game, and he may need to throw the ball a ton against a high-powered Lions offense that has scored 31 points in every game in 2026. The Lions’ defense has struggled against the pass (27th in EPA/Pass), so Dave Canales’ offense should look to the air in Week 4. No team in the NFL has allowed more passing yards than Detroit (898), and Young has easily cleared this total even in a loss to Cleveland. I’m buying the former No. 1 overall pick, as he looks to have turned a corner a bit in his fourth NFL season.

In fact, he leads all quarterbacks in completion percentage over expected at +10.9%. He had a slow Week 1, but completed 27 passes for 247 yards against the Packers and 31 passes for 321 yards against the Lions. Let's bet on that trend to continue against the Bears. David Montgomery OVER 10.5 Receiving Yards (-117) In his props article for Cowboys vs. Texans, Ryan Gilbert broke down why he likes David Montgomery to go over his receiving yards total of 10.5: David Montgomery is being used in the passing game a bit more in Houston than he was in Detroit, where Jahmyr Gibbs was the main back there. The veteran has caught all seven of his targets this season for 48 yards, going OVER 10.5 in all three games. Montgomery isn’t going to get a ton of targets, but he’s caught multiple passes in each game thus far, with 19, 14, and 15 receiving yards. I expect him to keep that going against this Cowboys defense that allowed 40 receiving yards to Rachaad White two weeks ago.
